The picks

Chosen for the recipient and use described, using published product information. We have not hands-on tested these products.

  1. 1. Adult builders with space for a long display model

    LEGO Icons Concorde

    For a patient builder with display space, the activity is as much of the gift as the finished airplane.

    An evening project that becomes a permanent part of their aviation corner. A strong choice for someone who loves airliners as much as flying them.

    Keep in mind
    The long finished model needs substantial display space, and an adult building kit is not a quick activity.
    Before you choose
    Allow a long display shelf: the finished model measures 41.5 inches. Ages 18+.
    $199.99Listed 2026-10-20View at LEGO↗
  2. 2. Airport-radio listeners and plane spotters

    ATC — Live Air Traffic Radio

    Our app: Pilot Gift Guide is produced by the team behind ATC. This is a recommendation of our own product.

    For someone who already enjoys following airport activity, a listening experience adds something new without adding more gear.

    Live airport audio with aircraft maps, transcripts and replay in one iPhone app.

    Keep in mind
    Coverage varies by airport; a subscription is not automatically transferable as a gift.
    Before you choose
    iPhone with iOS 18 or later; check airport coverage and current plans.
    Subscription; see current plansListed 2026-10-21Explore ATC↗
    Official App Store details ↗
  3. 3. Peanuts fans and nostalgic aviation lovers

    Peanuts Flying Ace Snoopy, 8-inch

    For the aviation lover who prefers a playful keepsake to technical equipment.

    The goggles and scarf give a familiar character a clear aviation connection.

    Keep in mind
    A decorative plush will not appeal to someone asking for practical flying gear.
    Before you choose
    Eight-inch sitting plush; surface clean only and check age labeling for a child.
    $39.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  4. 4. Pilots who take paper notes

    SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

    For the practical recipient, a useful small tool is easier to get right than an expensive electronics upgrade.

    Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

    Keep in mind
    Its utility is limited for someone who keeps all notes digitally.
    Before you choose
    Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.
    $24.50Listed 2026-10-20View at Pilot Mall↗
  5. 5. Pilots with a personal connection to the Cessna 172

    Cessna 172 Skyhawk model

    Especially personal when the Cessna 172 was the airplane they learned in.

    The best model is often the aircraft with a story behind it. This mahogany Skyhawk is especially thoughtful for someone who learned to fly a Cessna 172.

    Keep in mind
    A finished display model offers no building activity; choose a kit if assembling it is part of the appeal.
    Before you choose
    Confirm their aircraft type. A 172 and a 182 are different airplanes, even if they look similar.
    $249.00Listed 2026-10-20View at Pilot Mall↗
  6. 6. Readers interested in aviation art and WWII history

    Bomber Boys: WWII Flight Jacket Art

    Choose this for the reader interested in the people and artwork of aviation history.

    Photography of original flight jackets connects design, aircraft crews and personal history.

    Keep in mind
    The premium coffee-table format is a larger purchase than a paperback memoir.
    Before you choose
    Check format and shelf space; this is visual history rather than flight instruction.
    $129.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  7. 7. Pilots decorating an office or hangar

    Trintec 14-inch Altimeter Wall Clock

    A fit for an office or hangar whose owner likes instrument-inspired design.

    An instrument-inspired face brings aviation into a room without another aircraft model.

    Keep in mind
    Fourteen inches is substantial wall décor and may not match their room.
    Before you choose
    Uses one AA battery; check wall space and mounting needs. It is a clock, not an instrument.
    $41.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  8. 8. Pilots looking for a compact backpack-style flight bag

    Flight Gear Stealth Bag

    For a pilot who has specifically asked for a compact backpack-style flight bag.

    A flight bag is a gift they can use beyond the holidays. This compact backpack-style option is worth a look when their current setup is an overflowing ordinary bag.

    Keep in mind
    A compact flight bag may be too small for a pilot who carries a full day’s equipment.
    Before you choose
    Compare the listed dimensions with their headset, tablet and usual load before choosing.
    $79.95Listed 2026-10-20View at Sporty’s↗
  9. 9. Airshow visitors and race fans

    Owala FreeSip 24 oz, Roswell Air Races

    For the air-race fan who would use a bottle on ordinary days as well as at the airshow.

    A familiar everyday bottle gains a specific connection through air-race branding.

    Keep in mind
    The branded version costs more than many plain bottles.
    Before you choose
    Check cup-holder fit; the retailer specifies hand-washing the bottle.
    $50.00Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  10. 10. Frequent flyers and holiday gift exchanges

    Kurt Adler Airliner Ornament

    A modest seasonal gift that can carry a story about a favorite trip.

    A small passenger-jet ornament is easy to personalize with a travel memory.

    Keep in mind
    Resin can be fragile and the appeal is seasonal.
    Before you choose
    Approximately 4.75 inches; decorative ornament, not a child’s toy.
    $7.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗

How we ranked these ideas

We prioritize personal appeal, usefulness and how easily someone outside aviation can confirm the right fit. That puts a recognizable display model or a practical everyday accessory ahead of equipment that requires an exact aircraft configuration. A recipient’s own wishlist should always take precedence over a general ranking.

Choose for their kind of aviation

Collectors may enjoy a building project or a model of a meaningful aircraft. Student pilots may appreciate a small useful accessory, after checking what their school supplies. Working pilots often have strong equipment preferences, so ask before choosing anything for the cockpit.
